answer: Settled weight is an anchor that cannot move while the chain watches. Each identity's payout weight is pinned to the earliest blocks it mined, and a comet beacon samples old anchors at random epochs, demanding the original storage receipt. Restoring one means replaying its whole history, and the k-th restore an operator performs costs k squared in bond, so n fresh heads pay nearly n cubed to look old. Each anchor also sends a pulse every epoch; a silent one loses priority, and buying priority back is priced per operator, not per head, so one shared history buys one anchor of trust, never n.
